title: Admission control & geo-QoS for Redwood Relevance: priority queuing and graceful fallback
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The relevance/reranking endpoint has experienced tail-latency spikes during global traffic surges. Current single-stage throttles and broad circuit breakers either allow SLO violations or cause large tenant-wide failures. We need an admission-control layer with tiered queues, geo-aware routing decisions, and a lightweight fallback selection path to keep high-priority traffic within latency budgets while preserving overall throughput.

Scope: implement an admission controller in front of the relevance service that provides: (1) tenant-level priority queues and queue-shedding policies, (2) region-aware routing based on real-time SLO headroom, (3) dynamic, per-model graceful fallback rules (e.g., lower-cost embedding-only scoring when full reranker times out), (4) metrics, dashboards and alerting for queue depth, shed-rate, and per-tenant p95/p99 latency.

Out-of-scope: model retraining or changes to ranking model architecture. Dedicated capacity autoscaler tuning is a follow-up (see deps).
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller deployed as a sidecar or gateway rule in front of the relevance service in two regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1).
Per-tenant priority queues implemented: low/normal/high with configurable weights and hard limits; documented API to set tenant priority.
Queue-shedding policy that drops low-priority requests deterministically when p95 predicted breach > configured latency budget, with immediate metrics emitted.
Geo-aware routing: traffic routed to region with available headroom; if none, fast fallback model invoked. Routing decision latency < 2ms added to request path.

Fallback selection: choose compatible lighter-weight scoring path (embedding-based cosine rerank or cached top-k) within the same request to produce best-effort results when full rerank cannot meet SLO.
Dashboards display per-region headroom, queue depths by priority, shed-rate, fallback-rate, and correlated p95/p99 for both full rerank and fallback paths.
Runbook created and oncall run through with the SRE team; at least one synthetic workload test that reproduces shedding behavior in staging.
tasks: Design admission-controller API and config (PRD link in links).
Implement queueing primitives in gateway: priority queues, token bucket enforcement, and deterministic shedding logic.
Integrate region headroom signal from runtime metrics (cpu/gpu util + recent p95) and build routing policy engine.
Add fallback adapters in the service to call embedding-only scorer or cached top-k when signaled by controller.
Build dashboards and SLO alerts, add synthetic test harness for shedding and fallback validation.
Run internal load test (gradual ramp) to validate behavior and collect perf numbers for rollout playbook.
decisions: Implementation as a lightweight Envoy filter vs. sidecar: we will prototype as an Envoy Lua filter for minimal latency, with a path to sidecar if logic grows.
Fallback default: embedding-similarity scorer with configurable threshold. Chosen because embeddings path is already available and has predictable lower latency.
Queue-shedding policy: deterministic oldest-lowest-priority-first drop instead of randomized sampling to provide consistent degraded behavior for tenants.
risks: Routing decision adds extra hop latency; risk mitigated by implementing highly-optimized headroom check cache and minimizing RPCs.
Tenant misconfiguration of priority could result in accidental denial for important customers; will add guardrails and audit logs.
Fallback output quality may not satisfy all product features; must surface quality regressions and provide easy opt-out for customers.
